title: Space Tech Briefing — September 27, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! It's September 27th, 2026, and you're tuned into your daily dose of cosmic innovation and discovery! I'm your host, ready to launch you into the latest and greatest from beyond our atmosphere.

As we eagerly anticipate today's new launches and breakthroughs, let's take a moment to recap some truly monumental recent developments from the past week. First up, we're highlighting a shining example of international collaboration in space science. French expertise is once again taking center stage! The far-infrared camera, PRIMAger, has been officially selected by NASA as one of the two crucial instruments for the upcoming PRIMA mission. This selection truly underscores the cutting-edge French know-how in far-infrared technology, a testament to the incredible work by experts at CNES, the French space agency. It's fantastic to see such specialized knowledge contributing to global scientific endeavors!

And speaking of major recent discoveries, how about this for a lunar landmark? Scientists have just unveiled the largest impact crater discovered on the Moon in a century! Using incredible imagery from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, or LRO probe, researchers pinpointed a massive new crater. It measures a staggering 222 meters in diameter, surrounded by an expansive seven-kilometer-wide 'cold spot.' This colossal scar on the lunar surface has been officially named in honor of the late American scientist Tom McGetchin, a geologist and planetologist renowned for his work on impact craters. The impact itself was relatively recent, occurring between April 11th and May 22nd, 2024, when an asteroid or comet, estimated to be the size of a three to six-story building, slammed into the lunar surface. The crater is approximately 43 meters deep, a truly monumental testament to the dynamic forces shaping our celestial neighbor!

What a journey through the cosmos this morning! From cutting-edge instruments to monumental lunar impacts, the universe is always serving up something extraordinary. Thank you for joining me on this space odyssey. Stay curious, keep looking up, and we'll connect again soon for more exciting updates from the final frontier!
